description: From fz-t93.26's paper (M4). The rescue handler reads Raisable through uses.read (jobs/semantic.rs ~1219, raisable_ty) instead of waiting on it. Raisable only grows, so the handler is analysed at each step of the exception union and every step leaves a contribution row behind; the final plan depends on job order. Shows on 00795 and 00796 (Enum.into(list, %{})). Done when the handler waits on the finished Raisable and 00795/00796 plans are identical under fifo and lifo (fz-t93.26's cfg(test) order knob). Evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/t93_26/.
title: A rescue handler waits for the exception type it rescues
